# External Validation Case 001 — PX4 #27879

## Source

- Upstream issue: https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/27879
- Platform: CubePilot Cube Orange+
- PX4: v1.17.0 stable
- Public crash ULog A: `02a49fdc-6e69-4aba-8439-e18259c65ebb`
- Public crash ULog B: `f2cdb24d-3d6d-44de-8912-ea618e465811`
- ULog B SHA-256: `29a40039eda7ecb0c388075c8b104ce5e5e5b2f59dbb47ec5172fc83b5095a73`

## Ground truth

The upstream issue was later traced to a PX4 software hardfault path involving `MavlinkCommandSender::initialize()` re-initializing a shared semaphore while in use, corrupting NuttX priority-inheritance holder state. The fix was associated with PX4 PR #27606 / commit `b1a17ac355` and was recommended for backport to the 1.17 branch.

## Consistency check

Both independent crash logs from the same upstream incident family produced the same material conclusion under the frozen v0.1 baseline: no telemetry-observable material root event was selected.

## Interpretation

**Result: FAIL / out-of-scope software hardfault for the current v0.1 telemetry-only root-cause reconstruction scope.**

This is a useful counterexample rather than a benchmark to tune against. The confirmed upstream cause is a software/concurrency hardfault in the MAVLink/NuttX path, while PAMIR v0.1 currently selects roots only from a focused set of continuous flight-telemetry families. The hardfault metadata and fault-log execution context are not part of the v0.1 root-selection input.

The two-log consistency check strengthens the product-boundary finding: PAMIR is not randomly missing one file; the current v0.1 evidence surface does not expose this confirmed software root.

> PAMIR v0.1 can reconstruct telemetry-observable failure chains, but it does not yet reconstruct software hardfault roots that are visible primarily through PX4 hardfault/fault-log metadata rather than continuous flight telemetry.

## Integrity rule

Do **not** tune v0.1 to force this case to pass. Keep the validated v0.1 baseline frozen. Any support for software-hardfault evidence should be evaluated in a separate post-v0.1 lane with explicit tests and false-positive controls.
